subject: Cooking
title: Belgian Frites: The Fry Origin War
description: A quick win: understand Belgian Frites: The Fry Origin War.

hook.text: They're called 'French fries' worldwide. Belgium insists they're Belgian. The argument has raged for centuries.

buildup.text: Belgians claim villagers in the Meuse valley fried potatoes in the 1680s when rivers froze and fish was scarce.

discovery.text: American soldiers in WWI encountered frites in French-speaking Belgium — and called them 'French' fries.

twist.text: Belgium's secret: double-frying. First at 300°F to cook through, then at 375°F for the crispy golden exterior.

climax.text: Belgium has more frite stands per capita than any country — and submitted frites to UNESCO for heritage status.

punchline.text: French fries are Belgian. The name is the world's most stubborn mistake.

quiz.question: Why are Belgian frites called 'French fries' in English?
options: WWI soldiers encountered them in French-speaking Belgium

details.summary: Belgium and France both claim to have invented fried potatoes, fueling a rivalry that has lasted centuries. Belgians insist they were frying potatoes along the Meuse River in the 1680s when frozen rivers forced them to fry potatoes instead of fish.
details.whyItMatters: The frites origin dispute shows how food becomes national pride. Belgian double-frying in tallow produces a demonstrably superior product that challenges the French claim.
takeaways: Belgium claims frites originated along the Meuse River in the 1680s
Double-frying in beef tallow creates the signature Belgian crunch
The term 'French fries' may be a linguistic miscommunication

faq.question: Why are they called French fries if Belgium claims them?
faq.answer: One theory says American soldiers in World War One encountered frites in French-speaking Belgium and called them French fries. Another says 'French' referred to the cutting technique called frenching. The name stuck in English despite Belgian objections that persist to this day.

faq.question: Why does double-frying produce better frites?
faq.answer: The first fry at lower temperature cooks the interior through and creates a starch layer on the surface. The second fry at higher temperature crisps that starch layer into a rigid, golden shell. The result is crispy outside, fluffy inside — impossible to achieve with a single fry.
